requirements.note: Three-column grid of rounded HSL squares with the emoji centred, newest first, under a tile count. The grid sits below a large custom header (eyebrow, serif title, tagline, filter card), so it starts about a third of the way down the screen.
A wide card opens a system menu with All boards plus the ten boards and a checkmark on the current one. Filtering works (Coast shows 64 tiles).

Large view shows title, board chip and 'Added October 26, 2026'. It is a real paging collection: the page follows the finger, a short drag snaps back, and 'n of N' in the nav bar updates. The prev/next buttons also work. Opened from Liked, it pages through liked tiles only.
A big Like/Liked button in the detail view toggles the like. The Liked tab shows the same grid with heart badges, and its count updates after like and unlike.
Select puts check circles on tiles and offers Select all. A bottom panel has Like and Delete. Delete asks for confirmation in an alert ('Delete 2 tiles?'). Bulk like works and leaves select mode.
After relaunch: 598 tiles, the likes kept, Liked count 65.

bugs: At the largest text size the main screen in select mode shows no tiles: the huge header, wrapped 'All boards' card, 'Select all' and the tall bottom action panel take up the whole screen, and 'Select all' is cut off behind the panel.
At the largest text size the detail view's 'Added …' date line is hidden behind the bottom Like bar.
tells: Custom web-like header (letter-spaced eyebrow caption, serif display title, tagline) instead of a navigation bar with a large title. It scrolls away with no nav bar left behind.
Board filter is a hand-drawn full-width card with its own chevron, not a toolbar menu button or segmented control.
Select mode shows '3 selected' and 'Done' twice: in the header and again in a custom bottom panel with big pill buttons, instead of a system toolbar.
Liked tab icon is always drawn filled, even when not selected.
Custom cream/green palette and pill buttons throughout, which reads as a designed web or React Native look rather than system styling.
At large text the header blocks reflow badly ('All boards' wraps onto two lines inside the card, and Select drops onto its own line), pushing the grid far down.
Grid emoji do not scale with Dynamic Type (fine), but the header does, without limits.
A.scroll: Smooth: no blank or popping tiles during flings, a normal rubber-band past the top, and the scroll position is kept on returning from the detail view. The grid's content frame grows lazily as you scroll, which you can't see.

requirements.note: Edge-to-edge three-column grid with 1–2 pt gutters, newest first, starting right under the nav bar. The emoji are small (about a quarter of the tile) at default size.
A filter button in the nav bar opens a system menu (Boards header, All Boards plus ten, checkmark). The title becomes the board name and the subtitle shows the count (Coast, 64 tiles).

Detail shows a full-width square, title, board and date, with prev/next buttons and an 'n of N' label. The swipe is a gesture that swaps the tile: the page does not follow the finger, and a short slow 60 pt drag already jumps to the next tile. Opened from Liked, it pages through liked tiles only.
A heart button in the nav bar toggles like. The Liked tab uses the same grid, its count updates, and an unliked tile disappears from the list after going back.

Select turns the title into 'N Selected' and adds Like and Delete buttons in the nav bar, with system-style blue check circles. Delete asks for confirmation in an alert. Bulk like works and leaves select mode.
After relaunch: 598 tiles, the likes kept, Liked count 65.

bugs: Detail swipe triggers on a short drag and does not track the finger. It feels like a gesture recogniser rather than paging, so an accidental small horizontal drag changes the tile.
tells: The swipe between tiles is not interactive paging: the content doesn't move with the finger and there is no snap-back.
The nav title jumps from leading-aligned ('Moodboard') to centred ('Coast', 'Liked') depending on the screen or filter.
The detail view's like heart is black (not tinted or red) when liked, while the grid uses red heart badges.
The detail view's nav title is just 'Tile', and prev/next are hand-drawn grey circle buttons in the content.
At the largest text size the grid emoji scale up until they overlap the selection circles, and the select-mode title truncates to '1 Selec…'.
Tab label 'All Tiles' uses a photo icon, which is fine. Overall the look stays close to system defaults.
B.scroll: Smooth: no blank or popping tiles mid-fling, a normal bounce at the top, and the scroll position is kept after opening and closing a tile.

why: Both meet every requirement and keep their state across relaunches. A has the better detail pager (true paging with snap-back) but wraps everything in a custom, web-like header and bottom panel, which falls apart at large text (no tiles visible in select mode). B looks and behaves much closer to a stock iOS app: nav-bar menu, nav-bar select actions, edge-to-edge grid. Its main flaws are a non-interactive swipe and some large-text truncation.
